steps.intent: France’s objective is to secure a timely, legally robust renewal of the maritime arms-embargo inspection authorization before it lapses, while responding to the 12 May Tripoli clashes with a balanced call for de-escalation, UNSMIL support and full implementation of the ceasefire, including withdrawal of foreign forces and mercenaries. The main difficulty will be preserving the narrow consensus behind resolution 2733 (2024): Russia and China may abstain or seek to dilute flag-State consent, reporting and withdrawal language, and some members may resist new burdens on the Government of Libya. We will keep the text close to the existing inspection framework and avoid new sanctions or naming individual States so that it can attract at least nine votes without a veto.

Add: 'Reaffirming that measures to implement the arms embargo, including any maritime inspections, must be consistent with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya.'

Add at the end: 'and requests the Secretary-General to report to the Council within 90 days on progress, including the identified remaining foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries and steps taken for their withdrawal.'

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft's focus on de-escalation and a Libyan-led political process, but we cannot accept OP7 as drafted. Any maritime inspection must rest on the prior express consent of the flag State and be closely coordinated with the Government of Libya and UNSMIL, consistent with international law and Libyan sovereignty. We also seek a time-bound report on the withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries.
messages.China: China supports a balanced text focused on de-escalation, protection of civilians and a UN-facilitated Libyan-owned political process. However, OP7 as drafted authorizes high-seas inspections without prior flag-State consent and risks impinging on sovereignty and freedom of navigation. China asks the penholder to strengthen the safeguards in OP7 and add language ensuring that the authorization does not affect Libya’s sovereignty or normal oil exports; otherwise China would find it difficult to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the direction of the draft and its focus on de-escalation, protection of civilians and full implementation of the arms embargo. We ask that the text include the standard humanitarian carve-out recalling resolution 2664 (2022), making clear that humanitarian assistance is not restricted. We would also like a reference to resolution 2744 (2024) and due process, including the focal point for delisting. With those additions, Denmark can support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft as a co-sponsor and welcomes its balanced focus on de-escalation, the political process and the arms embargo. We ask that the text reinforce implementation at sea, including through cooperation with regional maritime operations such as EUNAVFOR MED IRINI, and reaffirm respect for maritime rights under international law, including UNCLOS. These changes are important for Greece given the Mediterranean dimension of arms trafficking, migration and maritime security.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft’s reaffirmation of the arms embargo, de-escalation, protection of civilians and full implementation of the 2020 ceasefire, as well as its strong support for UNSMIL. Our principal concern is OP7: Guyana abstained on resolution 2733 (2024), and we would need express prior flag-State consent and explicit UNCLOS compliance for the maritime inspection authorization. With that adjustment, Guyana is prepared to support the text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft’s reaffirmation of Libya’s sovereignty and the UN-facilitated Libyan-led political process, and we can support the renewal of the maritime arms-embargo inspection authority. We ask the penholder to tighten OP7 so that inspections are clearly grounded in international law, coordinated with the Committee, and limited strictly to the arms embargo rather than migration control. We also request a preambular reference to the non-punitive nature of the asset freeze and the preservation of frozen assets for the Libyan people, consistent with our position on resolution 2769 (2025).
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft’s focus on de-escalation, the arms embargo and UNSMIL. As a maritime State, we need OP7 to state explicitly that inspections, seizures and disposal are conducted in full conformity with UNCLOS and with due regard for flag-State rights, and that implementation does not unduly interfere with lawful commercial shipping or humanitarian assistance. We also ask for a preambular safeguard that measures are not intended to have adverse humanitarian consequences and that Libya’s resources benefit the Libyan people.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France and Greece for the draft and supports its overall direction, including the renewed high-seas inspection authorization. To strengthen legal clarity and consistency with our prior position, we ask that OP7 expressly place inspections under international law, including UNCLOS, and that the text include a humanitarian carveout paragraph recalling resolution 2664 (2022). We believe these adjustments preserve the draft’s balance and reinforce Council unity.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the political and ceasefire elements of the draft, but the current text remains unbalanced on enforcement and external interference. We cannot accept an open-ended maritime inspections regime; it must be strictly limited, consensual with the flag State, coordinated with the Libyan Government and not authorize the use of force or destruction. We also ask for clear language upholding Libya’s sovereignty and rejecting external interference in its internal affairs.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft's core objectives, particularly de-escalation, protection of civilians and full implementation of the arms embargo. We ask that OP7 make the 1970 Committee's central role in disposal explicit, consistent with our earlier position that the Committee should lead on how seized items are disposed of; without this, we would have difficulty supporting the text. We also seek the designation reminder in OP6 and a reference to the 5+5 JMC and the two Chiefs of Staff. We can be flexible on the reconciliation-law reference.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of the maritime inspection authorization and the draft’s political message. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP2 with an explicit accountability and investigation element, and OP7 with clear international law and human rights safeguards. We also seek a reference to resolution 2664 (2022) on humanitarian carve-outs and a minor addition on women’s and youth participation in OP3.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the thrust of this draft, which is consistent with resolution 2769 and the need for a Libyan-led political process. We ask the penholder to strengthen coordination for high-seas inspections and to add explicit support for Libyan counter-terrorism and regional reconciliation efforts, in cooperation with the African Union and the League of Arab States.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft’s core objectives, including renewed maritime inspection authority and full implementation of the arms embargo. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text by condemning recent violence and calling for accountability, by adding operative follow-up to resolution 2769 on illicit petroleum exports and designations, and by explicitly supporting 5+5 military and security reunification. We can support the text with these changes.
messages.United States of America: The United States appreciates France and Greece’s work and supports the draft’s core objectives on de-escalation, UNSMIL, the ceasefire and the arms embargo. We ask the penholders to add a focused counterterrorism and border/maritime security reference consistent with resolution 2769, strengthen the petroleum language to cover fuel smuggling and illicit imports, and add an accountability call for the 12 May Tripoli clashes. We can work flexibly on placement, but these elements are important for US support and for the text’s credibility.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates all key red lines, especially by conditioning maritime inspections on prior express flag-State consent, limiting them to six months, excluding force and adding Committee approval for disposal. It also incorporates accountability, humanitarian carve-out, 5+5, counterterrorism and petroleum measures, aiming for consensus.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the revised text. Our key concerns on prior express flag-State consent, a six-month limit subject to review, close coordination with the Government of Libya and UNSMIL, and reporting to the Council are now reflected in OP13. We will vote in favour of the resolution.
messages.China: China welcomes the penholder’s incorporation of prior flag-State consent, UNCLOS, the no-force understanding and safeguards for Libya’s normal petroleum exports. However, the phrase 'to or from Libya' goes beyond the arms embargo and risks interfering with lawful Libyan exports and maritime rights. Limiting the scope to vessels bound for Libya would align paragraph 13 with the embargo and with Libya’s sovereignty; with that adjustment, China would be prepared to support the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised text and welcomes the inclusion of our prior requests on resolution 2664 humanitarian exemptions and resolution 2744 due-process language. One remaining concern is that OP13’s express-consent requirement risks weakening the maritime arms embargo compared with prior Council authorizations. We would ask the penholder to align the inspection provision with the established 'good faith efforts' standard while retaining all existing safeguards and human-rights protections.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on land, sea and air cooperation, the explicit IRINI reference, and Mediterranean maritime rights. We stress that the maritime inspection authorization must be implemented strictly in accordance with UNCLOS, with express flag-State consent and solely for arms-embargo enforcement. Greece is ready to vote in favour and calls on all Council members to support a unified text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and has no further requests. We welcome the incorporation in OP13 of express prior flag-State consent and explicit conformity with UNCLOS, which address our earlier red line. We encourage all Council members to support adoption of the text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan welcomes the incorporation of its proposals concerning UNCLOS, Committee coordination, the arms-embargo limitation, and the asset-freeze paragraph. We support the current text and encourage all Member States to respect Libya’s sovereignty and fully implement the arms embargo and the 2020 ceasefire. Pakistan remains committed to a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the revised draft, which is balanced and consistent with our priorities: it reaffirms UNCLOS, flag-State consent, safeguards for lawful commercial shipping and humanitarian assistance, and keeps sanctions targeted. We appreciate the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier requests and encourage the Council to preserve those elements and proceed to adoption.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France and Greece for the revised text and for incorporating our earlier concerns on UNCLOS and flag-State rights and on the resolution 2664 humanitarian exemption. We believe the current text strikes an appropriate balance between strengthening the arms embargo and respecting Libya’s sovereignty, freedom of navigation, and humanitarian access. The Republic of Korea therefore supports the draft as it stands and encourages the Council to send a unified message on Libya.
messages.Russian Federation: We acknowledge that key Russian concerns on sovereignty, flag-State consent and non-use of force are now reflected. However, we cannot support language that gives a Security Council imprimatur to a specific EU naval operation; this is outside the Council’s proper role and risks politicizing implementation of the arms embargo. We request deletion of the IRINI references in OP13 and OP14 and neutral wording on regional arrangements, in coordination with the Government of Libya. With those changes, we are ready to support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised text. We welcome the incorporation of Committee approval for disposal, the designation reminder, and the references to the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and the national reconciliation law, which address our earlier concerns. We encourage all members to unite behind this balanced text and call on Libyan parties to engage with UNSMIL and implement the ceasefire and arms embargo.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the revisions, which incorporate our previous requests on accountability, human-rights and refugee-law safeguards, and women/youth participation. We support the text as presented and urge the Council to send a unified message on de-escalation, protection of civilians, and full implementation of the arms embargo and ceasefire. We encourage all members to vote in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft and appreciates that our priorities on Libyan sovereignty, regional coordination, counterterrorism support, and AU/LAS-facilitated reconciliation have been reflected. We believe the text strikes a balanced approach and should be put to the vote.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the incorporation of our key asks on accountability, 5+5 reunification and implementation of resolution 2769 (2025). We remain concerned that OP13’s requirement for the flag State to have expressly consented prior to inspection is stricter than the existing Council authorization and risks undermining Operation IRINI and the arms embargo. We ask the penholder to align OP13 with the established “good faith efforts to first obtain consent” language; with that change, we are ready to support the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised text and appreciates the penholders' incorporation of our earlier requests. We remain concerned that OP13's requirement for express flag-State consent and Committee pre-approval of disposal would weaken the maritime inspection regime compared to prior resolutions. We ask that OP13 restore the standard 'good faith efforts' consent language and replace Committee approval of disposal with coordination, to ensure the arms embargo can be enforced effectively.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: retained review, GOL/UNSMIL coordination and reporting; OP13 consent aligned with prior Council language to preserve unity.
replies.China: partially accepted: retained to/from scope but added an explicit limit for outbound inspections to arms violations and protection for lawful petroleum exports.
replies.Denmark: accepted: OP13 now uses the established good-faith efforts standard while retaining safeguards.
replies.Greece: partially accepted: retained UNCLOS, maritime-rights and arms-embargo limits; adjusted IRINI and consent language for consensus.
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: retained UNCLOS and commercial-shipping safeguards; consent standard aligned with prior resolutions.
replies.Panama: partially accepted: retained UNCLOS and commercial-shipping safeguards; consent standard aligned with prior resolutions.
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: no changes requested; humanitarian and UNCLOS safeguards retained.
replies.Russian Federation: accepted: removed IRINI references, adopted neutral regional-arrangements wording, and adjusted OP7 reporting language.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: OP13 now uses good-faith efforts language consistent with prior resolutions.
replies.United States of America: accepted: OP13 uses good-faith efforts language and Committee coordination for disposal.

steps.summary: The penholder accommodated the P5 requests on good-faith consent, Committee coordination, neutral regional-arrangements language and OP7 reporting, while preserving safeguards for lawful petroleum exports. The text should secure broad support with no P5 negative vote; expected abstentions are China, Algeria, Guyana and Panama.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria's stated negotiation position was support, and the draft contains core Algerian priorities on sovereignty, Libyan-led process, AU coordination, and withdrawal of foreign forces; any residual concerns over OP13 are handled through an explanatory statement rather than a negative vote.
reasons.China: China's core concern on OP13 was largely addressed by the added limits on outbound inspections and protections for lawful petroleum exports, and the overall text aligns with China's support for Libyan sovereignty and a political settlement; voting in favour is consistent with its prior positions and interest in Council consensus.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark’s key request on OP13 was accepted, and the resolution reinforces the arms embargo, ceasefire implementation, humanitarian access, accountability and UN-led political process in line with Denmark’s policy. Denmark therefore votes in favour.
reasons.France: France is the penholder and co-sponsor, and the draft aligns with France’s established support for Libya’s sovereignty, the arms embargo, UNSMIL, and a Libyan-led political transition. As a permanent member and author, France would vote in favour and speak in support before the vote.
reasons.Greece: Greece is a co-sponsor and its priorities—UNCLOS, maritime rights, arms embargo, and balanced inspections—are reflected, so it would vote in favour and explain its support.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana had signalled support and its priorities—sovereignty, UNCLOS safeguards, humanitarian access, and a Libyan-led political process—are reflected in the draft. A yes vote is consistent with its recent votes in favour of renewing and strengthening the Libya sanctions and political mandate.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan had already indicated support and did not request changes; the draft reflects its priorities of Libyan sovereignty, UN-facilitated political dialogue and safeguards around maritime inspections. Voting in favour is consistent with its earlier support for resolution 2769 (2025).
reasons.Panama: Panama supports the draft because its maritime-inspection provisions include key UNCLOS and flag-State safeguards, consistent with Panama's support in the last negotiation round. Abstaining or opposing would be inconsistent with Panama's recorded support and maritime-law priorities.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported Council action on Libya’s arms embargo, political process and humanitarian safeguards, and it had already signalled support for this draft in the last negotiation round. The text retains the safeguards on maritime inspections that align with ROK’s emphasis on UNCLOS, no use of force and humanitarian carve-outs.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia's key requested amendments on neutral regional wording and OP7 reporting were accepted, making the text acceptable despite remaining concerns over maritime inspections. Voting yes supports a balanced, sovereignty-focused resolution while preserving Russia's constructive role in the Libyan political process.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone had already indicated support, and the draft addresses its prior A3+ concern by strengthening coordination with the 1970 Committee while including sovereignty, no-force, maritime and humanitarian safeguards.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia was already in support during negotiations and has consistently voted for Libya resolutions focused on the arms embargo, UN-led political process, ceasefire implementation and civilian protection. The draft reflects those priorities while containing acceptable legal safeguards, so Slovenia votes yes.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia was recorded as supporting the draft and made no requested changes; voting in favour is consistent with its emphasis on Libyan sovereignty, UN-facilitated political solutions, African coordination, and full implementation of the ceasefire and arms embargo.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft aligns with the UK’s priorities on Libya, including support for UNSMIL, the arms embargo, accountability, and the political transition, and the UK’s key requested change on OP13 was accepted. There are no red lines requiring opposition or abstention.
reasons.United States of America: The draft aligns with U.S. policy supporting Libyan-led political progress, full implementation of the arms embargo, and accountable security sector reform, and the penholder accepted the key U.S. change to OP13. No provision warrants abstention or veto.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank France and Greece for their efforts. We support the text’s reaffirmation of Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, and its emphasis on an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process under United Nations facilitation. We welcome the references to coordination with the African Union and the League of Arab States on national reconciliation and transitional justice, and the call for the withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries. At the same time, we stress that any authorization for high-seas inspections under operative paragraph 13 must be implemented in strict conformity with international law, including UNCLOS, with due respect for the sovereignty and maritime rights of States and the consent of flag States, without the use of force, and must not be used for migration control or to interfere with Libya’s lawful petroleum exports. Algeria supports this resolution in the interest of Council unity and the stability of Libya, while reaffirming the need to avoid all external interference and to preserve Libya’s national resources for the benefit of its people.
before.China: (spoke in Chinese): China supports a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process and respects the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Libya. We have taken note of the improvements in the draft regarding maritime inspections, including the explicit limits on outbound inspections to arms embargo violations, the protection of lawful petroleum exports, the requirement of flag State consent and the clarification that nothing authorizes the use of force. China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We hope that the authorization will be implemented strictly in accordance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and will not affect normal commercial shipping or humanitarian assistance. The international community should continue to support United Nations mediation and encourage the Libyan parties to resolve their differences through dialogue and consultation.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We strongly support Libya’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and the UN-facilitated, Libyan-led political process aimed at free, fair and inclusive elections and a unified government. We condemn the recent violence in Tripoli and underscore the need for de-escalation, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access and accountability. We welcome the resolution’s reaffirmation of the arms embargo, the 23 October 2020 ceasefire commitments, including the withdrawal of foreign forces, fighters and mercenaries, and the humanitarian safeguards consistent with resolution 2664 (2022). Denmark also welcomes the revision to paragraph 13, which now reflects the established good-faith efforts standard and retains essential safeguards under international law, including UNCLOS. Denmark remains committed to fair and clear procedures, including through the delisting focal point, and will continue to support the UN Support Mission in Libya and all efforts to advance a peaceful, inclusive and stable future for the Libyan people.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution, which it has submitted together with Greece. The text responds to the grave developments in Tripoli, reaffirms the arms embargo, supports UNSMIL and the Libyan-led political process, and strengthens maritime implementation while respecting Libya’s sovereignty and lawful petroleum exports. We call on all Council members to support this text and on Libyan actors to de-escalate, protect civilians, and return to dialogue, elections and unified institutions.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this draft resolution, which it has co-sponsored. We welcome the balanced text that reaffirms Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, supports the UN-facilitated Libyan-led political process and the holding of free and fair elections, and demands full implementation of the arms embargo and the 23 October 2020 ceasefire, including the withdrawal of foreign forces, fighters and mercenaries. We especially value the clear reaffirmation of international law, including UNCLOS, and of the maritime rights of all States in the Mediterranean. The carefully framed maritime inspection authorization must be implemented in full conformity with international law, with respect for flag States and without undue interference with lawful commercial shipping, petroleum exports or humanitarian assistance. Greece also stresses the need to protect migrants and refugees, counter human trafficking and smuggling, and ensure accountability for recent violence in Tripoli. We call on all Libyan actors to de-escalate and engage in good faith with UNSMIL.
before.Guyana: Guyana votes in favour of this resolution. We support its reaffirmation of Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, its emphasis on a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, and its call for full implementation of the arms embargo and the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement. We welcome the safeguards retained in the text, including respect for UNCLOS, the requirement of good-faith efforts to obtain flag-State consent before inspections, the explicit exclusion of any authorization for the use of force, protection of lawful petroleum exports, and full respect for humanitarian exemptions. Guyana urges all Libyan actors and institutions to de-escalate, protect civilians, engage constructively with UNSMIL, and work in good faith towards elections and the formation of a unified Libyan government.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our support for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, and for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations. We stress that all international efforts, including maritime inspections authorized by this resolution, must be exceptional, temporary, fully consistent with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and respectful of Libya’s sovereignty and maritime rights. Such measures must not be used for migration control or unrelated purposes. Pakistan calls on all Libyan actors to pursue de-escalation, national reconciliation and genuine dialogue, and on all external actors to cease interference and support the full implementation of the ceasefire, including the withdrawal of foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries. We support the role of UNSMIL and the 5+5 Joint Military Commission and urge the Council to remain focused on a sustainable, Libyan-owned political settlement for the benefit of the Libyan people.
before.Panama: Panamá votará a favor de este proyecto de resolución. Como Estado de pabellón y firme defensora de la Convención de las Naciones Unidas sobre el Derecho del Mar, valoramos que el texto conserve garantías esenciales: el consentimiento de buena fe del Estado del pabellón, la prohibición del uso de la fuerza, la protección del comercio legítimo y de la asistencia humanitaria, y la limitación estricta de estas autorizaciones a la implementación del embargo de armas, sin que puedan utilizarse para el control migratorio. Apoyamos los esfuerzos para estabilizar Libia, proteger a su población y avanzar hacia un proceso político libio, inclusivo y soberano. Interpretaremos y aplicaremos el párrafo 13 de manera estricta y conforme al derecho internacional, incluidos los derechos de los Estados del pabellón y la libertad de navegación.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France and Greece for their efforts to facilitate the Council’s deliberations. We remain deeply concerned by the clashes in Tripoli on 12 May 2025 and by the continued fragility of Libya’s security situation. The Republic of Korea supports a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations Support Mission in Libya, and we call on all Libyan actors to exercise restraint, protect civilians and ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access. We also support full implementation of the arms embargo and the 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement, including the withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries from Libya. In particular, we welcome the safeguards in paragraph 13: prior notification, coordination with the Government of Libya and the Committee, good-faith efforts to obtain flag State consent, full conformity with UNCLOS and applicable human rights and refugee law, no authorization of the use of force, and no interference with lawful petroleum exports or humanitarian assistance. On this basis, the Republic of Korea votes in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that a number of our substantive concerns were taken into account, in particular the removal of references to specific European Union maritime operations and the adoption of neutral language on regional arrangements. We emphasise that any implementation of the arms embargo, including possible inspections on the high seas, must be conducted in strict compliance with international law, in full respect for the sovereignty and maritime rights of Libya and flag States, and must not be used for migration control or any purposes unrelated to the arms embargo. We also stress that the resolution must not serve as a pretext for external interference in Libya's internal affairs. The only sustainable path remains an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process under United Nations facilitation, without external interference. We call on all Libyan actors to engage constructively and on all Member States to support the ceasefire, including through the withdrawal of foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries in coordination with the Government of Libya and neighbouring States. The Russian Federation remains committed to a sovereign, independent, unified and prosperous Libya.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone welcomes the balanced and carefully framed text before the Council and will vote in favour. We support its reaffirmation of the arms embargo and the central role of the 1970 Committee, including in the coordination of inspection, seizure and disposal arrangements, which responds to a key concern long expressed by the A3+. The text also contains important safeguards: it is not a migration-control measure, it does not authorize the use of force, it respects Libya’s sovereignty and maritime rights, it protects lawful petroleum exports and commercial shipping, and it preserves humanitarian exemptions. At the same time, Sierra Leone remains deeply concerned by the fragility of the security situation, including the clashes in Tripoli and the continued flows of arms and foreign fighters. We call on all Libyan actors to engage in good faith under United Nations auspices, implement the 2020 ceasefire in full, protect civilians, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and move towards free, fair, transparent and inclusive elections that allow the Libyan people to determine their own future.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this resolution. We remain firmly committed to Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, and to an inclusive, Libyan-led political process facilitated by the United Nations. We support the Council’s clear messages on full implementation of the arms embargo, implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire, the withdrawal of foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, accountability, and the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth. We also stress that all measures, including maritime inspections, must be implemented fully in accordance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and must never be used for migration control or other purposes. Slovenia will continue to support the Libyan people and all efforts towards a unified, stable and peaceful Libya.
before.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholders for their efforts and welcomes the balanced text before the Council. Somalia supports this resolution because it reaffirms Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, and because it backs a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations. We strongly support the calls for de-escalation, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, national reconciliation, and full implementation of the 23 October 2020 ceasefire, including the withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries. We also stress that all measures, including maritime inspections, must be implemented in full respect for international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the sovereignty and maritime rights of States, and must not interfere with lawful petroleum exports or humanitarian assistance. Somalia values the resolution’s coordination with the African Union and the League of Arab States, and urges all Libyan actors to engage in good faith towards free, fair and inclusive elections and a unified Libyan government. Somalia will vote in favour.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank France and Greece for their work and welcome the constructive engagement that has strengthened the text, including the good-faith language on flag-State consent in paragraph 13, consistent with previous resolutions. The United Kingdom remains deeply concerned by the clashes in Tripoli and the continued fragility of Libya’s security situation. This resolution rightly calls for de-escalation, protection of civilians, accountability, full implementation of the ceasefire and the arms embargo, and renewed support for UNSMIL and the Libyan-led political process leading to free and fair elections and a unified Libyan government. We urge all Libyan actors to engage in good faith and refrain from unilateral actions that deepen divisions.
before.United States of America: The United States welcomes this resolution and thanks France and Greece for their work. We are pleased that the text reflects our proposed changes to ensure maritime inspections and seizures are implemented in accordance with international law, including the law of the sea; preserve necessary flexibility for good-faith efforts to obtain flag-State consent; and focus squarely on enforcing the arms embargo, not on migration control. This resolution sends a clear message that violations of the arms embargo, illicit oil smuggling, and the continued presence of foreign forces and mercenaries in Libya must end. We call on all Member States and Libyan parties to comply fully, and we vote in favour.

after.France: Thank you, Mr. President. France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which it presented together with Greece. The Council has sent a clear and united message: the clashes in Tripoli and all acts of violence must stop; Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity must be respected; and the only sustainable path is an inclusive, Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by UNSMIL, leading to free, fair, transparent and inclusive presidential and parliamentary elections as soon as possible and to a unified Libyan government. France calls on all Libyan actors and institutions to de-escalate, protect civilians, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, engage constructively and without preconditions with UNSMIL, and refrain from unilateral actions that deepen divisions. The arms embargo must be fully implemented by all Member States and all Libyan parties. The 23 October 2020 ceasefire agreement must be implemented in full, including the withdrawal of all foreign forces, foreign fighters and mercenaries without further delay. We stress that the maritime inspection authorization in paragraph 13 must be implemented strictly in accordance with international law, including UNCLOS, with good-faith efforts to obtain flag-State consent, without authorizing the use of force, and without affecting lawful petroleum exports, commercial shipping or humanitarian assistance; it is not a migration-control measure. France remains committed to working with all Council members, Libya’s neighbours and regional partners in support of Libyan-owned reconciliation and accountability. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and will continue to support UNSMIL and the Libyan people.
